name: Darryl Rawlings
current_role: Founder and Chair of the Board, Trupanion, Inc. (stepped down as CEO; Margi Tooth became CEO)
profile: Canadian-born founder of Trupanion, the Seattle-based medical insurer for cats and dogs. He started it in 1998 as Vetinsurance International, covered its first pet in Canada in 2000, entered the U.S. in 2008 and took it public on Nasdaq in July 2014. After handing the CEO role to Margi Tooth he remains Chair of the Board.
interesting_fact: When he was 14, his family dog Mitzy needed surgery his parents could not afford, and they left the vet hospital without her; he vowed pets would someday have better medical insurance than people do.
deep_cut_fact: Trupanion's very first insured pet (2000) was Darryl's own mixed-breed dog, Monty. He is also a founder of NAPHIA (North American Pet Health Insurance Association) and a graduate of the British Columbia Institute of Technology.
notes: No longer CEO (Margi Tooth CEO); signed the 2026 shareholder letter as Chair. Trupanion's annual shareholder letters are written in his voice and are a good conversation hook. NAPHIA/BCIT details also on sbxsf.trupanion.com/about/darryl-rawlings.

name: Russell A. (Chip) Childs
current_role: President & CEO, SkyWest, Inc. (St. George, Utah)
profile: Russell 'Chip' Childs runs SkyWest, the largest U.S. regional airline group, which flies for United, Delta, American and Alaska. A former audit manager, he joined SkyWest in 2001 as VP-Controller, was President/COO of SkyWest Airlines 2007-2014, and became CEO of SkyWest, Inc. in January 2016.
interesting_fact: He chairs the U.S. DOT/FAA NextGen Advisory Committee and sits on the Salt Lake City branch board of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco; under him SkyWest was named one of Fortune's Most Admired Companies.
deep_cut_fact: Before aviation he spent five and a half years in public accounting as an audit manager doing SEC reporting for large corporations; he holds a BYU economics BA and MAcc and has sat on BYU Marriott School's National Advisory Council since 2017.
notes: Low personal media profile; speaks mainly on pilot shortage / 1,500-hour rule and regional capacity. Go via SkyWest Corporate Communications.

name: Christopher M. Gorman
profile: Banker who has led KeyCorp, a ~$190bn-asset regional bank with ~18,000 employees and 3.5m clients, as Chairman and CEO since May 2020. He came to Key in 1998 via its acquisition of McDonald Investments, ran KeyBanc Capital Markets and Key Corporate Bank, led the First Niagara integration, and was COO before taking the top job.
interesting_fact: He led Key's integration of First Niagara Financial Group, the largest acquisition in KeyCorp's ~200-year history, and later took over as CEO in the middle of the Covid-19 pandemic.
deep_cut_fact: As a kid he ran 'a bunch of businesses'; a single weekend visit sold him on Miami University in 1979 ('I just really, really liked the people at Miami'). He has said he worked for five employers in his career, three of which became part of KeyBank. He sits on Miami's Farmer School Board of Visitors.
notes: Laura Mimura is the first-listed Key Corporate Communications media contact (page lists others by topic; Lisa LoParo covers Finance/Technology/Risk). Also chairs the Ohio Business Roundtable and is Vice Chair of the Cleveland Museum of Art.

name: Craig H. Stevenson Jr.
current_role: Director, International Seaways, Inc. (re-elected June 2026); Director, American Bureau of Shipping
profile: Veteran tanker-shipping executive. He joined OMI Corporation in 1993, rose to Chairman and CEO and oversaw its 2007 sale, then founded Diamond S Shipping (DSS LP) in 2007 with First Reserve, took it public in 2019 and merged it into International Seaways in July 2021, where he remains a board member.
interesting_fact: He has built and sold two U.S.-listed tanker companies: OMI Corporation (sold 2007) and Diamond S Shipping, whose 2021 merger with International Seaways created one of the largest U.S.-listed tanker fleets.
deep_cut_fact: He studied business administration at Lamar University in Beaumont, Texas, and was non-executive Chairman of Intermarine, one of the world's largest project-cargo carriers, from 2008 to 2018, as well as Chairman of Ship Finance International (now SFL) in 2007-2009.
notes: Non-executive director; no personal public channels found. International Seaways lists Tom Trovato as its Investor Relations & Media contact. 2026 board re-election per INSW 8-K (June 2026).

name: Solomon Moshkevich
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Natera, Inc. (named Nov 2026; previously President, Clinical Diagnostics)
profile: Natera veteran who joined the cell-free DNA testing company in 2011 after Bain & Company and Parthenon Capital. As first GM of Oncology he built the Signatera MRD cancer-recurrence business, became President, Clinical Diagnostics in Sept 2023, and in November 2026 succeeded Steve Chapman as CEO and joined the board.
interesting_fact: He helped develop Natera's flagship cfDNA tests (Panorama, Prospera and Signatera) and was the company's first general manager of oncology before being promoted straight to CEO after 15 years at the company.
deep_cut_fact: He sits on the board of Ronald McDonald House Charities of the Bay Area, and holds BA degrees in Economics and Mathematics from Columbia plus a Stanford MBA. He has called Signatera's CE mark the first ever for a bespoke (personalized) assay.
notes: Brand-new CEO (Nov 2026) - likely in high demand. Has done podcasts/interviews on MRD testing (MedTech Dive, AJMC, The Dr. Pat Show). Natera media contact listed as Lesley Bogdanow, VP Corporate Communications.

name: Philip G. Franklin
current_role: Independent Director (Audit Committee chair), TTM Technologies; Trustee, XAI Octagon Floating Rate & Alternative Income Trust (retired CFO)
profile: Retired finance executive. He was at circuit-protection maker Littelfuse from 1998 to 2016, ending as EVP and CFO, after CFO roles at OmniQuip International (which he helped take public), Monarch Marking Systems and Hill Refrigeration. He has served on the board of PCB and RF maker TTM Technologies since November 2010.
interesting_fact: From 2014 to 2021 he was a director of Tribune Publishing (Chicago Tribune), chairing its Audit Committee and later serving as non-executive Chairman of the Board.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of the Scholarship Foundation of Santa Barbara (Executive and Investment Committees), and holds an economics BA and an MBA from Dartmouth's Amos Tuck School.
notes: Retired, board-only role; low public profile. Only company channels (TTM IR / corporate marketing) are published. Nominated for re-election as class II director at TTM's 2026 annual meeting.

name: Glenn A. Pushis
current_role: CEO, McBride Capital Partners 'Project Aero' (planned titanium manufacturing facility in North Carolina); consultant to Steel Dynamics (retired as SVP Special Projects Oct 1, 2025)
profile: Purdue-trained engineer who came from Nucor and joined Steel Dynamics in 1994, helping build its first mill in Butler, Indiana. He ran SDI's long-products group and then, as SVP Special Projects, built the Sinton, Texas flat-roll mill and the 650,000-tonne recycled-aluminum mill in Columbus, Mississippi, before leaving in 2025 to lead a new titanium venture.
interesting_fact: He led construction of SDI's Sinton, Texas flat-rolled steel mill, the company's largest capital investment, and then its low-carbon recycled aluminum flat-rolled mill in Columbus, Mississippi; Mark Millett credited him as 'instrumental' to SDI's greenfield growth.
deep_cut_fact: He is a past president of the Association for Iron & Steel Technology (AIST), sits on the AIST Foundation's scholarship committee, received AIME Honorary Membership in 2020, and earned his Indiana University MBA in 2013 while already a senior SDI executive.
notes: No longer an SDI officer; now heading a titanium manufacturing start-up (Project Aero, McBride Capital Partners) - strong fit for an energy/industrial podcast. No published personal or Project Aero contact found; SDI only publishes an IR phone line (+1 260 969 3500).

name: Paul A. (Paul Anton) Zevnik
current_role: Chair of the Board, Entravision Communications Corp.; Senior Counsel, Miller Friel PLLC
profile: Harvard-trained lawyer and co-founder of Entravision, the Spanish-language media and digital advertising company, which he formed with Walter Ulloa and Philip Wilkinson. A director since its 2000 NYSE listing and Chair since 2023, he also spent 50 years in law, retiring as a Morgan Lewis partner in 2024; he is now Senior Counsel at Miller Friel.
interesting_fact: He was the founding and managing partner of a national law firm with offices in eleven cities that combined with Morgan Lewis, where he became Global Practice Area Leader for Product Liability, Tort and Insurance.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond Entravision he has helped form and finance media businesses spanning TV and audio production, digital/streaming and the use of spectrum for wireless communication. He holds Harvard degrees: AB magna cum laude and AM (both 1972) and a JD cum laude (1976).
notes: Low media profile. Best routes are Entravision IR (Roy Nir / Mark Boelke) or his law practice at Miller Friel PLLC (Washington, DC). The spectrum and wireless angle could connect to data/telecom themes.

name: Scott Marlette
current_role: Co-founder, GoodRx; former partner at Slow Ventures (stepped back from venture capital); no current operating role found
profile: Early Facebook engineer and product manager (c. 2005-2010) who co-founded GoodRx, the prescription-drug price comparison and coupon platform, in Santa Monica in 2011 with Doug Hirsch and Trevor Bezdek. He joined Facebook-alumni seed fund Slow Ventures as a partner in 2016, then stepped back from VC; GoodRx went public in 2020.
interesting_fact: At Facebook he started as an engineer and is credited with building Facebook Photos, later overseeing Groups, Events and Inbox as a product manager.
deep_cut_fact: Slow Ventures was nicknamed the 'Facebook Alumni Fund', backed by five early Facebook friends. When he stepped back, managing director Kevin Colleran said he was taking time off from VC and 'may eventually start another company of his own like he did previously with GoodRx.'
notes: Very low public profile; no verified personal site or social accounts found. Facebook Photos credit comes from Crunchbase (aggregator); verify before citing. Possible warm routes: Slow Ventures (slow.co) or GoodRx co-founder Doug Hirsch.

name: Prakash Janakiraman
current_role: Visiting Partner and Head of the AI Accelerator, The House Fund (from June 2026); Co-founder Emeritus, Nextdoor
profile: Co-founder of Nextdoor, the neighborhood social network. He was its Chief Architect and later Head of DEI and Belonging until 2022, and the company listed via SPAC in 2021. A former Google Maps engineering manager, he has been an angel/LP investor and in June 2026 joined UC Berkeley-focused VC The House Fund to run its AI accelerator for Berkeley founders.
interesting_fact: Before Nextdoor he spent nearly three years at Google managing engineering teams for Google Maps and Google Base.
deep_cut_fact: He is from Hayward, California, and went back to UC Berkeley to complete a BA in Sociology after co-founding a multibillion-dollar company. House Fund founder Jeremy Fiance called him one of the first LPs to believe in the fund.
notes: Most active route is The House Fund (AI accelerator, Summer '26 cohort). House Fund appointment confirmed via New India Abroad (citing his LinkedIn post), June 2026. The website value is the fund's site, not a personal one. No verified personal email found.

name: Philip Krim
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Montauk Climate / Montauk Capital (climate and energy venture studio, New York)
profile: Co-founder and longtime CEO of Casper, the direct-to-consumer mattress brand he launched in 2014, took public in 2020 and sold to private equity in 2021. He then 'got bit by the climate bug', incubated home-battery installer Haven, and in March 2024 co-founded Montauk Climate with Evan Caron and Sharo Atmeh: an $8.5M venture studio that builds its own climate-infrastructure and energy-transition companies.
interesting_fact: Montauk Climate doesn't take outside ideas: 'We author the businesses that we want to create,' Krim told TechCrunch, describing a studio that conceives energy-transition companies and then recruits teams to run them.
deep_cut_fact: In his University of Texas dorm room he taught himself HTML and built a mini-empire of e-commerce sites selling everything from sports tickets and poker software to window blinds and mattresses. That business sold about 40,000 beds before Casper existed.

public_contacts.value: montauk@moxiegrouppr.com (Moxie Communications Group, for Montauk Climate)

notes: Excellent fit for an energy/entrepreneurship podcast: he is very podcast-friendly (How I Built This, Awarepreneurs 'electron economy' episode) and speaks often on climate entrepreneurship. Pitch via Moxie PR. The 40,000-bed figure is from TechCrunch (techcrunch.com/?p=963396).
